page_note: No cosmological substrate present on this page. Page is entirely editorial: opens with disciples blessing the Apostle (dialogue frame), praising him for revealing the works and commandments of Elect-ship and teaching the catechumens 'degree by degree' (ecclesial institution), then transitions to a new disciple-question concerning converts who committed prior sins (idolatry, false doctrines, blasphemy, murder, adultery, magic, false witness) before being made disciples — will these 'first sins' be released for them when they enter the Church as Elect or catechumens? This is pure pastoral-ecclesial casuistry framed in apostolic Q&A. The seam flag at i=14 confirms institutional vocabulary cluster. Heavy damage (76.7%) but the surviving framework is unambiguously editorial. Teaching purity 0.000 is correct.

segments.temporal_note: Frame: 'when his disciples heard these sayings from him' — pure narrative attribution.
Disciples bless and glorify the Apostle — hagiographic frame.
Vocative 'our Father, you are glorious and blessed' — direct address to Mani figure.
'we receive the hope set for us through your hand' — Mani-mediated soteriology, hagiographic register.
'To the Elect indeed' — explicit institutional category. Score confirms.
'works and commandments of the Elect-ship' — ecclesial discipline language.
Introduces 'the catechumens' — second ecclesial tier.
'you did not lift your hand from them, but you taught them by degree' — pastoral pedagogy of catechumenate.
'degree by degree, in the Spirit and with decrees' — graded catechetical instruction.
'each one according to his [power]' — capacity-graded ecclesial pedagogy.
'reach the country of the Living Ones' — soteriological destination but framed as outcome of catechumen progress, not as cosmological mapping.
'Now also we beseech you, our Lord' — formulaic petition opening, no cosmological content.
'declare unto us concerning this saying' — request formula, refers back to prior teaching, no new substrate content survives.
'concerning the man who shall...' — opens the casuistic question about converts. Heavily damaged.
'come into the Church as elect [or]' — seam flag fires; institutional vocabulary cluster (ekklesia + elect).
'as catechumens — the first sins which they did' — opens the casuistic question.
'before they had been made disciples — shall they reach this end?' — pastoral question about pre-conversion sins.
'serving idols formerly, worshipping' — describes pre-conversion practice of converts; one side maps to the editor's contemporary religious landscape.
'reverencing the [idols/gods]' continues; transitions to others 'standing fast in the teaching of the doctrines' — ⲛⲁⲟⲅⲙⲁ marks rival sects.
'in the teaching of the doctrines, blaspheming against God' — ⲇⲟⲅⲙⲁ + blasphemy = polemical characterization of rival religious doctrines.
'blasphemed also the other Illuminators in the heavens' — polemic against opponents of Manichaean cosmology. ⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ is cosmological but the frame is accusatory.
'sinned with other sins' — continues catalogue of pre-conversion sins.
'murder, or a sin of adultery' — pastoral catalogue of sins.
'sin of magic, or false witness' — pastoral catalogue continues.
'these (sinned) in the evil works of the cosmos' — pastoral framing of pre-conversion sins.
'in them formerly. Now at the moment when' — temporal pivot to conversion question.
'of God, will they release for him' — penitential/forgiveness question.
'the first [sins], or not? Will they not be released for him?' — explicit casuistic question about absolution of pre-conversion sins.
'that you may reveal to us' — petition formula closing the question.
'and set our heart at rest' — disciples' closing petition formula.
